How to Measure AI ROI in a Commercial Team

Explainerlowob research

By lowob · 22 August 2026 · 5-minute read · Revenue

AI return on investment in a commercial team is the money gained from decisions and work the AI informed, minus what it cost to run, including the time people spend reviewing its output. It cannot be read from seats activated or hours saved. It is measured by attaching a value at stake to each decision when it is made, writing back the realised value later against a comparison, and netting off tool cost and review time. That is Gateway 2 in lowob's Build Order.

What AI ROI means in a commercial team

The arithmetic of return on investment is simple: gain minus cost, divided by cost. The difficulty is the gain. A drafting agent produces emails. A research agent produces account briefs. Neither is money until it changes a decision that moves money: a deal pursued or dropped, a discount given or refused, a renewal saved.

So measurement stalls. Teams report what is easy to count, and finance discounts it, because a draft is not revenue.

Level of measureExampleWhat it tells youWill finance accept it?
AdoptionSeats active, prompts sentPeople are using the toolNo
Time savedSelf-reported hours saved per weekPossible capacity releasedRarely; it is an estimate and the time is not banked
OutputDrafts produced, briefs writtenVolume of workNo, unless tied to an outcome
Decision valueMargin retained, deals won, renewals saved, against a comparisonMoney changed by decisionsYes, if the comparison is credible

Why most firms cannot show a return

The surveys agree on the outcome, if not the cause. PwC's survey, published in January 2026, found 56% of CEOs had seen no significant financial benefit from AI. IBM's Institute for Business Value, surveying 2,000 CEOs between February and April 2025, found a quarter of AI initiatives had delivered expected ROI. The MIT NANDA report The GenAI Divide, covered by The Register in August 2025, claimed 95% of organisations had seen zero return; it drew on 52 interviews, a survey of 153 people and a review of over 300 public initiatives, so treat it as directional.

One reading is that the tools do not work. Another, which fits what lowob sees in client briefs, is that most firms never set up the arithmetic. Success measures are written as adoption or time saved, with no link to a decision that moved money.

If about half of generative AI spending sits in sales and marketing, as the MIT report found, that is where the measurement gap costs most.

A build that cannot state its value will be cancelled by someone who can state its cost.

How to measure it

The method is set out in full in Gateway 2: Put a Dollar Figure on Every Commercial Decision. In brief, it needs four things.

StepWhat it involvesWho owns it
1. Record the decisionThe commercial decisions the AI informs, with reason, owner and expected outcomeDeal or account owner
2. Set value at stakeOne number when the decision is made, using a definition agreed with finance per decision classFinance defines, owner fills in
3. Write back against a comparisonRealised value at the check date, compared with a matched group of similar decisionsRevenue operations
4. Net the costSubtract tool cost and the loaded cost of review and write-back timeFinance

Three points make the difference between a number finance accepts and one it ignores.

The comparison. A discounted deal that closes looks like a win. If standard-price deals in the same segment closed at the same rate, the discount bought nothing. Without a comparison group, AI gets credit for outcomes that would have happened anyway.

Review time. For a system where people approve drafts and check records, human minutes are usually a larger cost than tokens. lowob's measure is reviewer minutes per useful decision, tracked against a baseline set before launch.

Leading and lagging. In long sales cycles, report value at stake and the share of records with outcomes written back each quarter, and realised value when outcomes land. Do not present a quarter's figure as final.

Common mistakes

  1. Counting hours saved as money. Hours saved are only money if they are redeployed to something measured, or if headcount changes.
  2. Crediting the agent. The record shows a decision was informed by the AI's preparation, not that the AI caused the outcome. Credit the decision.
  3. Changing the definition every quarter. Keep each value-at-stake definition stable for at least two quarters, or comparisons reset.
  4. Tying pay to it too early. If individual pay depends on recorded value in the first year, people choose which decisions to record.

lowob takeaways

  • Measure decisions, not activity. Seats and prompts describe adoption, not return.
  • Value at stake first. Set one number when the decision is made, defined with finance.
  • Always compare. Realised value means little without a matched group.
  • Net off the people. Review time is part of the cost and often the largest part.

Common questions

How do you calculate the ROI of AI in sales?

Attach a value at stake to each decision the AI informs, record the realised value at a check date against a comparison group, then subtract tool cost and human review time and divide by total cost.

Why do most companies see no return on AI?

Surveys from PwC and IBM show most firms cannot point to a financial return. A common reason is measuring adoption or time saved instead of linking AI to decisions that move money.

Is time saved a good measure of AI ROI?

On its own, no. Time saved is an estimate, and it becomes money only if the time is redeployed to measured work or reduces cost.

How long before AI shows a return in a commercial team?

Expect two quarters of recorded decisions and outcomes before a credible figure. In long sales cycles, realised value may take a year.

Sources and notes

  • PwC, PwC 2026 Global CEO Survey, 19 January 2026. Self-reported survey of 4,454 CEOs in 95 countries and territories.
  • IBM, IBM Study: CEOs Double Down on AI While Navigating Enterprise Hurdles, 6 May 2025. Vendor-run survey with Oxford Economics; IBM sells AI services.
  • MIT NANDA, The GenAI Divide: State of AI in Business 2025, as reported by The Register, 18 August 2025. Small sample; secondary report of the study.

Pick one commercial decision class that your AI tools touch, such as discount exceptions. Agree with finance this week how its value at stake is defined, and start recording it on every new decision.
